requirements.requirement: Run a containerized web application on node1 as the unprivileged account appsvc, serving on port 8080
requirements.summary: appsvc created as unprivileged uid 1000 (cmd-cdf7bcfec05a4413); rootless podman installed and used by appsvc to run nginx:alpine bound to host port 8080 via pasta rootless port forwarding (cmd-661623ced35e4abb); verified with curl returning HTTP 200 and podman ps showing the running container (cmd-e5f7db3e26f44e8e). Post-restart snapshot also confirms port 8080 listening (global:after_executor:node1:listening-sockets).

requirements.requirement: Application starts at boot while the appsvc account has no active login session
requirements.summary: Linger was enabled for appsvc (cmd-cdf7bcfec05a4413) and a systemd --user unit (container-webapp.service) was generated and enabled (cmd-17f5caa4ea284a20, cmd-b87f5764e1a44ac2), with no login session present while it ran (cmd-b5cf002d9df1481e). A pre-restart baseline was captured (cmd-84eff60a27834a04, boot_id 67f3a44b...), a real reboot was executed and acknowledged before disconnect (cmd-4fb915c483234651, cmd-acdab9e488014cbb), and post-restart evidence shows a different boot_id (cmd-c516b237f000455a, 9a3aedf3...), corroborated by the fixed lifecycle boot-identity cross-check (global:before_prepare:node1:boot-identity vs global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity). After restart, loginctl showed no sessions for appsvc, container-webapp.service was active, the container had freshly restarted, and curl returned HTTP 200 (cmd-20f3d8dafc9d4704). This is a complete pre-restart/disruption/post-restart transition as required.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task — running a rootless containerized web app as appsvc on port 8080, and having it start at boot without an active login session — are directly and coherently demonstrated, including a genuine reboot with before/after boot_id proof, no-session confirmation, and a working HTTP 200 response after the restart. Operational hygiene is good, with only a trivial installation log left in /tmp and no unnecessary or unreverted risky mutations.
limitations: The after_prepare snapshot is an alias of before_prepare (prepare stage disabled), so preparer-vs-executor state separation relies entirely on the before_prepare vs after_executor comparison; this is adequate here since prepare was not used.
Only one reboot cycle was captured; no independent evidence exists for repeated or unexpected restarts beyond the single demonstrated transition.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed the executor timeline chronologically: dnf install of podman/shadow-utils, useradd+linger for appsvc, subuid/subgid confirmation, ad-hoc podman run for initial verification, stop/rm of that ad-hoc container followed by generating and enabling the systemd --user unit, pre-restart baseline capture, a background/acknowledged reboot, and post-restart verification. Every state-changing command maps clearly to either establishing a prerequisite, satisfying the material outcomes, or capturing bounded evidence. The one ad-hoc podman run/stop/rm cycle (cmd-661623ced35e4abb, cmd-b87f5764e1a44ac2) was a reasonable intermediate step toward the final systemd-managed container and left no residue (final podman ps shows only the systemd-managed instance). The only leftover artifact is /tmp/dnf.log from the package install, visible in the after-executor temporary-files diff — a low-risk, expected installation byproduct rather than an unnecessary mutation. No failed services, no unsafe exposure changes, and package-health checks remained clean before and after.
